text:
Vice Chairman Yoon Sang-hyun seeks to boost brand's market share through HK inno.N's distribution network Kolmar Group has secured the Korean distribution rights for Red Bull, the world's No. 1 energy drink brand, as Vice Chairman Yoon Sang-hyun seeks to capitalize on the fast-growing market by adding the Austrian brand to HK inno.N's business portfolio.
HK inno.N plans to leverage its nationwide distribution network and experience in building Condition, a popular Korean hangover relief drink, into one of the country's leading brands to expand Red Bull's market share.
Launched in Austria in 1987, Red Bull sold approximately 14 billion cans worldwide last year, up 10.2 percent from a year earlier. Its revenue rose 8.6 percent to a record 12.2 billion euros ($14.1 billion).
The global energy drink market is also expanding rapidly. According to market research firm Grand View Research, the market was valued at $85.3 billion last year and is projected to reach $158.5 billion by 2033, representing an average annual growth rate of 8.1 percent.
Korea's energy drink market is also growing strongly despite a slowdown in overall beverage consumption. Lotte Chilsung Beverage's energy drink sales rose 11 percent year-on-year to 107.2 billion won last year, while sales at convenience store chains GS25 and CU increased 26 percent and 18.3 percent, respectively.
Once consumed mainly by students studying late at night and office workers putting in overtime, energy drinks are gaining popularity among a broader range of consumers seeking an energy boost for exercise and outdoor activities.
According to Embrain Trend Monitor, domestic energy drink purchases rose 14.7 percent from April last year to March this year. Consumers in their 40s recorded the strongest growth at 21.7 percent, followed by those in their 20s at 19.1 percent and those in their 50s at 14.6 percent, indicating that demand is expanding beyond younger consumers.
Yoon sees considerable room for Red Bull to expand its presence in Korea despite its global dominance. The brand currently ranks third in the domestic energy drink market. He believes HK inno.N's sales expertise and nationwide convenience store network, developed through its success with Condition, can help strengthen Red Bull's market position. Yoon reportedly took part personally in the final stages of negotiations to secure the distribution rights.
This is not Yoon's first strategic move to identify new growth opportunities. HK inno.N, formerly CJ Healthcare, has expanded significantly since Kolmar Group acquired it in 2018. Its annual revenue has grown from the high 400 billion won range at the time of the acquisition to more than 1 trillion won last year.
A key growth driver has been K-CAB, a treatment for gastroesophageal reflux disease and Korea's 30th domestically developed novel drug. Launched in 2019, it recorded cumulative prescription sales of 1.04 trillion won in the first half of this year. HK inno.N has also signed export and licensing agreements covering 55 countries.
"Red Bull, the world's No. 1 energy drink brand, has struggled to fully realize its potential in Korea. Its partnership with HK inno.N could provide an opportunity to turn things around," an industry official said.
